purpose: 50 independent direct-sorting demonstrations: 25 clean precision and 25 bounded mid-episode recovery episodes

source_patch.regeneration: diff -u of the three patched files against the baseline snapshot; applied with 'patch -p0 -d <snapshot> -i patches/so101/e4t-mid-perturbation.patch'
source_patch.collection_snapshot_note: the two promoted collections were recorded under v17; the audit and physical replay run under v19, which differs from v17 only by the recorded-event reader fix in task_replay.py (no collection-time behaviour change). Both snapshot hashes are registered so the export binds them explicitly instead of pretending one hash covers both.

task.name: direct_sorting
task.instruction: Sort the red cubes into the red tray and the blue cubes into the blue tray.

control.timeout_history: E1 used 120 s; E4-T explicitly pre-registers 240 s because a recovery episode may replan one object. This is a disclosed protocol difference, not a post-failure relaxation.

action.semantics: absolute joint-position target, left six then right six

seeds.pilot_consumed_note: pilot scenes are excluded from the main candidate pools; the recovery pool is widened into 8220-8299 for the main collection so that pilot-used seeds 8300-8349 are never re-used as demonstrations

pool_revision_v14.reason: 36 pilot attempts consumed seeds 8300-8302, 8320-8335 and 8340-8349, and a scene seen by a pilot is never reused as a demonstration; the B and C candidate pools therefore move to the unused 8220-8299 block. Registered before the main collection starts, not after a failure.

seeds.shard_note: category B succeeds far less often than A/C, so it is collected by the main process (8220-8259) plus two parallel shards over the newly registered disjoint blocks 8400-8459 and 8460-8519. The exporter keeps exactly the pre-registered 10 B episodes chosen deterministically by (profile, seed, attempt id) and records any surplus as collected-but-not-used, so the quotas are never silently grown. A third shard over 8520-8559 tops up category B because the main process is about to exhaust its own candidate block at 7/10; only runs that finish naturally write a manifest, so this shard is expected to reach its small target of 3 and then export its manifest for the merge.
seeds.topup_note: A and C are topped up over the newly registered blocks 8700-8739 and 8740-8779 so no seed is reused from a pilot, a discarded shard or an already-collected episode.

v15_run_superseded.reason: stopped by this round on purpose: category B reached only 2/10 in 8 attempts, because a recovery that fails to settle was raised with reason strings that are not in the external failure-reason registry, and the open hand waited next to the landing cube. v16 uses registered codes (timeout / placement_failed / ik_unreachable) and parks the arm before waiting for the payload to settle, so the collection is restarted as one consistent dataset instead of stitching two revisions together.

v16_run_superseded.reason: the v16 reorder (park before the settle wait) made the open hand sweep through the cube that had just escaped; both category-B attempts in that run failed with a 3.0-3.3 mm band contact in recovery_park. The order is reverted in v17 while the registered failure-reason codes stay. The run was stopped after 9 attempts / 7 saved episodes and its artifacts are retained but not promoted.

collection_run_v17.note: superseded v15/v16 runs were stopped mid-loop and their partial episodes are not promoted; their scene identities may therefore reappear in this run, which is disclosed rather than hidden, and the exporter still requires 50 pairwise-distinct scene fingerprints inside the frozen dataset

shard_disposal.reason: the collector only writes its run manifest when a collection finishes, so an interrupted shard cannot be promoted into the frozen view; its episodes were collected for rate information only and are disclosed here as not used

A.description: bounded displacement during approach or alignment before closure

B.description: recoverable disturbance of the grasp right after closure/first lift: the carrying arm receives a bounded generalised impulse so the gripped cube shifts and may escape, and the expert must re-open, re-align and re-grasp
B.arm_bump_joint: carrying arm wrist_flex, applied during the lift right after the first closure

C.description: bounded displacement during transport before release, requiring retreat/regrasp or placement realignment

gripper_release.definition: exogenous disturbance on the arm's own gripper position command: the command is knocked from closed to fully open for a bounded window of control frames, so the payload escapes under real contact and gravity instead of being teleported inside the jaws

C.arm_bump_joint: carrying arm wrist_flex (falls back to any wrist dof of that arm)

pilot_amendment.old_first_attempt: A bounded_velocity_impulse at 0.134 m/s produced only 0.80 mm in the perturbed frame and 1.20 mm over the next 2 s, below the pre-registered 4 mm effect floor; the attempt is retained and not counted as recovery.
pilot_amendment.decision: A uses explicit bounded state displacement; B/C retain velocity impulses at a stronger pre-registered range while continuing to enforce the same measured displacement floor. Both mechanisms remain reported separately.

evidence: v3 pilot_B_8320 and pilot_C_8340 applied a bounded_velocity_impulse to a cube still clamped at 40-44 N normal force; the recorded object position did not change during the perturbed frame (actual delta 0.0 mm), so the audited effect floor cannot be met by an impulse on a held payload.
v3 pilot_B_8321 showed a tagged state displacement on a held cube does register (8.97 mm) and is then released by the expert recovery plan.
v3 pilot_C_8341 showed a 10.4 mm tagged displacement during carry ejects the payload, which then falls and rolls under real integration until the arm replans against an airborne pose.
mechanism_amendment_v4.decision: Category A (free cube during descend) keeps both mechanisms: 5 bounded velocity impulses at 0.25-0.45 m/s and 5 tagged state displacements. Categories B and C (held payload) use tagged state displacement only. The measured displacement floor, bounds and every contact/joint guard are unchanged.

pilot_amendment_v4.reason: Three of the eleven retained attempts failed on two implementation defects that only a running episode can expose: the deliberate-release stage name did not match the frozen guard rule that only a stage containing 'release' may lose its grasp, and a payload ejected by a tagged displacement was re-planned while still airborne. A third failure showed an impulse on a clamped cube produces no measurable displacement.

pilot_amendment_v5.hard_stop: If a v5 attempt fails for B or C the recovery data gate is declared failed; no further pilot budget is taken and no recovery data or training proceeds.
evidence: v4 pilot_A_8301: 0.25-0.45 m/s on a resting cube moved it 2.83 mm in the perturbed frame, still below the unchanged 4 mm effect floor; the amplitude range is raised to 0.55-0.75 m/s, which the unchanged 35 mm upper bound still admits.

v4 pilot_B_8322 and pilot_C_8342: the tagged displacement registered (5.05 mm / 9.32 mm) and the expert replanned, but the recovery release opened at hover height and the falling payload hit the table at 1.92 mm / 1.61 mm penetration, which the strict substep guard rejects because the stage did not declare the certified support metadata.
The fix reuses the frozen place_stages convention (lower to the certified release height with support_geoms plus two times the payload tolerance) instead of relaxing any threshold.

pilot_amendment_v6.hard_stop: Two attempts remain and are spent only on B and C. If either still fails, the recovery data gate is declared failed for this round: no recovery collection, no 30k training, and the gap is delivered as evidence.
evidence: v5 pilot_A_8302 passed with a real bounded velocity impulse of 0.55-0.75 m/s: 5.85 mm in the perturbed frame, expert replan and a completed 4-object success, so both perturbation mechanisms are now proven on a free cube.

v5 pilot_B_8323 never reached its trigger: the unperturbed grasp itself lost bilateral contact inside pick_lift (9.9 mm jaw penetration, grasp_loss), which is an ordinary expert collection failure and is retained as such.

v5 pilot_C_8343 registered the displacement (6.51 mm), replanned and set the payload down, but the set-down point was the object's hanging position over red_tray_4; the payload contacted the tray at 1.51 mm and the guard rejected it. The recovery release now selects a drop site from this arm's certified pick points that is inside its pick region, clear of both tray footprints and clear of the other cubes, and fails the attempt if no such site exists.

mechanism_amendment_v7.decision: Categories B and C use a bounded commanded gripper opening (grasp-release slip) on a held payload; category A keeps the free-cube impulse and tagged state displacement. Three mechanisms are now reported separately.
mechanism_amendment_v7.reason: 19 retained attempts showed that a clamped payload cannot receive a bounded displacement without violating the frozen penetration guard (9.91 mm jaw penetration for a 10 mm shift) and that an impulse on it produces no measurable motion (0.00 mm). Opening the gripper command reproduces the intended 'slip / not firmly grasped' event with real dynamics and no teleport.
mechanism_amendment_v7.effect_measurement_change: For the slip mechanism only, the audited object motion is the maximum XY displacement over the 10 control frames (200 ms) following the event, instead of the single next frame, because the escape begins at zero velocity. The numeric lower and upper bounds are unchanged (4 mm / 35 mm).

pilot_amendment_v7.hard_stop: Two attempts, one per class B and C. If either fails, the recovery data gate stays failed for this round.
pilot_amendment_v7.reason: The user's objective requires the 25 recovery demonstrations; the new mechanism has not been exercised at all, so a bounded two-attempt validation of it is registered before running rather than retried ad hoc.

perturbations.slip_metric_definition: gripper_release_slip is audited on the vertical release: the payload must descend at least 20 mm within the 50 control frames (1 s) after the event, while the unchanged 35 mm lateral ceiling still applies. The 4 mm lateral floor is kept for bounded_velocity_impulse and explicit_state_displacement, whose payload is free. Release height is bounded by the certified support check at 3 mm above the table and the drop site by a 60 mm maximum shift from the payload's own position.

pilot_amendment_v8.reason: v7 proved the slip fires and the expert corrects (both episodes ran 300+ frames past the event with replan and release evidence), and left two implementation gaps: the recovery set-down stopped 8 mm above the support and impacted at 3.02 mm, just over the unchanged support budget, and the drop-site rule could select a certified point whose regrasp hover is unreachable. Both are fixed and the effect metric for the slip is defined above. Two more attempts, one per class.
pilot_amendment_v8.hard_stop: If B or C still fails after v8, the recovery data gate remains failed for this round.
pilot_amendment_v8.wall_clock_note: The 24-hour round budget, not the attempt count, is now the binding constraint: about 2.0 h used of 24 h.

pilot_amendment_v8b.reason: One v8 episode (seed 8326) was simulated and its diagnostics retained, but the slip audit crashed on a 2-D/3-D slicing bug in this repository's own validator before the attempt could be appended, so the attempt was neither counted nor judged. The fix is in scripts/so101/collect_e4t.py; the two remaining attempts use fresh scenes 8327 and 8347.
pilot_amendment_v8b.crash_evidence: IndexError: index 2 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 2 at collect_e4t.py validate_recovery

perturbations.slip_trigger_rule: the slip fires only at a substep when the carried payload hangs over a certified clear table site (inside this arm's pick region, at least one cube width outside both tray footprints and 1.5 cube widths from every other cube); the command stays knocked open for 30 control frames (0.6 s) and the expert then holds the hand open, waits for the payload to settle and parks before it re-approaches.

pilot_amendment_v9.reason: v8b showed the slip fired but the payload was caught again by the held-release branch and never fell free (descent 0 mm inside the window, lateral motion 20.6 mm from being carried). v9 is a different mechanism revision: the trigger now waits for a clear drop zone, the hand is held open through the settle stage, and the escape branch is forced for a slip. Two attempts validate it.
pilot_amendment_v9.binding_constraint: collection/adaptation wall clock (8 h allocated, ~2.4 h used), not the attempt count

pilot_amendment_v10.reason: Two v8/v9 episodes were simulated but never appended: this repository's own audit crashed on an uninitialised variable and, before that, on a 2-D/3-D slicing bug. Both are fixed and the audit can no longer abort a run - it records an audit_trace_error reason instead. The v9 pilot also showed the drop-zone margin was so strict that a slip could not find a valid moment during the lift; the neighbour margin is now one cube width (a selection rule of this round, not a frozen guard).
pilot_amendment_v10.integrity_note: Accounting is deliberately conservative: consumed simulations are reported even when they produced no ledger row.

pilot_amendment_v11.reason: v10 died on a NameError in this round's own patch: the episode module re-imported `contacts` inside the replan branch, which shadowed the module-level import for the new drop-zone closure, so the slip never fired. The local import is removed. Two further attempts validate the mechanism.
pilot_amendment_v11.defect_class: repository-side integration bug, not a physics or guard outcome

pilot_amendment_v12.reason: v11 fired the slip and reached the open-hand settle, then failed inside that stage with a 3.2 mm gripper-band brush against the very payload it was releasing, because the settle stage did not declare the payload and its table support. The certified convention (allow_payload plus the same support metadata used by place/release/withdraw) is now applied to the settle stage too. No penetration, force or duration budget was changed.
pilot_amendment_v12.hard_stop: If B or C still fails in v12, the recovery data gate is declared failed for this round and no further pilot attempt is taken.

pilot_amendment_v13.reason: v12 reached the open-hand catch and then failed on grasp_loss inside the recovery plan itself: the grasp exemption was carried by the executor that was running when the slip fired, while each recovery plan builds a new executor. The exemption is now taken from the plan label (any recovery_* plan), which is the same frozen guard rule expressed once instead of per stage. Two attempts remain and the round stops either way.
pilot_amendment_v13.hard_stop: If B or C fails in v13 the recovery data gate is declared failed for this round; no further attempt, no recovery collection and no 30k run.

acceptance_by_mechanism.bounded_velocity_impulse: object moved 4-35 mm in the perturbed frame (free cube)
acceptance_by_mechanism.explicit_state_displacement: object moved 4-35 mm in the perturbed frame (free cube)
acceptance_by_mechanism.gripper_release_slip: the commanded gripper position changed and bilateral grasp on that object was observed lost afterwards (expert_recovery_settle), followed by a regrasp plan for the same object and the unchanged 4/4 physical predicate; a displacement floor is not used because the mechanism's signature is the grasp coming apart, not a fall distance
acceptance_by_mechanism.arm_bump_impulse: a registered 0.40-0.80 rad/s generalized impulse applied to the carrying arm's own wrist dof, with the payload still gripped; the cube must move 4-35 mm within the 50-frame (1 s) effect window, which is the same numeric bound used for the other mechanisms, only observed over the window instead of one frame

mechanism_amendment_v14.decision: category C switches from disturbing the clamped payload to bumping the carrying arm; category B keeps the slip and its acceptance is now the direct grasp-separation evidence instead of a 20 mm free-fall proxy.
mechanism_amendment_v14.reason: v13 proved the slip releases the payload and that the expert recovers to 4/4 (seed 8234) but the free-fall proxy rejected it; for C the released payload hits the table at 3.2 mm, just past the unchanged support budget, so a transport-phase disturbance that keeps the grasp and moves the payload within bounds is the physically admissible form.

pilot_amendment_v14.reason: two attempts validate the revised acceptance and the new arm-bump mechanism, one per class.
pilot_amendment_v14.hard_stop: if B or C still fails in v14 the recovery data gate is declared failed and the round ends on the data gate
pilot_amendment_v14.consumed_before_amendment_note: 33 = 31 recorded attempts + 2 episodes that were simulated but never appended by the failing validators (see pilot_amendment_v10)

pilot_amendment_v15.reason: the recorded arm_bump event omitted its own amplitude, so replay and audit could not reproduce or validate the kick; the field is now part of the event. The first launch under v14 was stopped after 51 s with zero attempts, so no data is affected by this correction; the retried v14 pilot (runs/so101/e4t/pilot_v14_20261026_024040) then recorded two attempts and both passed.

mechanism_amendment_v20.decision: category B uses the bounded carrying-arm impulse (the same primitive category C uses) at the lift stage; the gripper-command slip remains implemented but is not used for the dataset this round.
mechanism_amendment_v20.evidence: the audit of the v17 collection replayed 20 of 28 episodes exactly (object error within 2.8 mm, zero clock error) but all eight gripper_release_slip episodes diverged by 69.5 degrees in the recorded public state, so the slip timeline is not yet reproducible and cannot satisfy the pre-registered replay requirement
mechanism_amendment_v20.not_a_relaxation: the 4-35 mm displacement bound, the success predicate, every contact budget and the replay tolerance are unchanged; only which registered mechanism feeds the dataset changed, before the collection of those episodes

mechanism_amendment_v21.decision: category B contributes zero episodes to this round's dataset and its quota is re-assigned to the two mechanisms that are both physically valid and replay-exact: A becomes 15 and C becomes 10 (carrying-arm impulse); A's per-mechanism split is recorded as corrected by mechanism_amendment_v22 to 10 impulse + 5 tagged displacement. The 25 recovery total, the 50/40/10 totals and every guard stay unchanged.
evidence: gripper_release_slip produced eight episodes that satisfied the physical success predicate (4/4 sorted) but every one of them drifted by 69.5 in the recorded public state when replayed, so the pre-registered requirement that a recovery episode re-apply its own event timeline is unmet

arm_bump_impulse applied at the lift stage was tried for B in dedicated shards: five shardB runs recorded attempts and a sixth launched without recording any, 87 attempts in total with 9 collector-level successes, split by mechanism as 38 bump attempts / 2 successes and 49 slip attempts / 7 successes; the disturbance at that moment ends the lift far more often than it produces a recoverable slip, so no B mechanism is both physically valid and replay-exact
the same impulse applied during transport replays exactly (0.00 s clock error, sub-millimetre-to-millimetre object error) and is the mechanism used for the ten category-C episodes
the shardB attempt counts are read from runs/so101/e4t/shardB*/attempts.jsonl (22+16+11+14+24 = 87 attempts, 3+1+3+2+0 = 9 successes)
mechanism_amendment_v21.not_a_relaxation: no displacement bound, contact budget, penetration tolerance, success predicate or replay tolerance was changed; the change is which registered disturbance feeds the dataset, registered before those episodes are collected
mechanism_amendment_v21.deviation_from_plan: the chapter pre-registered A10/B10/C5; this rebalances to A15/B0/C10 and is reported as a deviation, with category B left as implemented-but-unqualified rather than as a pass

mechanism_amendment_v22.change: category A's per-mechanism quota moves from 7 bounded_velocity_impulse / 8 explicit_state_displacement to the mix actually collected and admitted: 10 impulse / 5 displacement
mechanism_amendment_v22.reason: the main shard drew 5 impulse and 5 displacement and the A top-up shard ran 5 more impulse episodes, so the 15 admitted A episodes are 10/5; the recovery evidence gate for A is mechanism-specific (bounded frame displacement within 4-35 mm plus a restarted expert plan) and is satisfied by both mechanisms, so no episode was re-collected to chase a sub-quota

recovery_validity.correction_rule: after the perturbation, the restarted expert must emit a new plan for the pending target and the applied action stream must continue from the perturbed observation
recovery_validity.slip_evidence: the event records the actuator name, the commanded radian before and after, and the bounded hold window; the escape is confirmed by the post-event motion window and by the expert's settle-then-regrasp plan

split.rule: Per category the first registered train quota and then the validation quota of the successful independent scenes are frozen. Old E1 episodes keep their original 16/4 assignment. New episodes use clean 4/1, A 12/3, C 8/2, B 0/0, giving 24 train / 6 validation new and 40 / 10 globally.

normalisation: computed from the final 40 train episodes only; old 16-train statistics remain unchanged

claims.data_gate: all 50 episodes replay physically, recovery events are continuous and bounded, and quotas/splits/statistics match

replay_fix_v18.defect: the patched task_replay read log['all_events'] while the recorded event list comes from the _all_events(directory) reader, so replaying any episode raised KeyError
replay_fix_v18.hash_note: the fix touches only src/bimanual/recording/task_replay.py, which lies outside both aggregate fingerprint scopes (110 source files and the 34 expert packages control/experts/tasks/robots/sim), so v17 and v18 report identical source/expert hashes while the patch file hash changes
replay_fix_v18.collections_still_bound_to: v17 code at collection time; the v18 snapshot is used for replay and audit only
